spacing.note: macro layout strictly 8-based; intra-component padding optical (3/5/6/10px)

taste.name: Borderless Depth
taste.trigger: When content blocks needed to read as distinct objects on a white page
taste.decision: Chose a 4-layer shadow with alphas ramping 0.01 to 0.04 over a 1px border, using no visible borders anywhere
taste.reason: A border is a drawn line the eye must parse as content; a shadow is light behavior the eye already knows to ignore, so readers register separation without registering that anything was added
evidence: only single-layer shadow is 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0) at zero alpha

taste.name: Accent Rationing
taste.trigger: When a brand blue was available for headings, links, icons, borders, and section backgrounds
taste.decision: Chose to spend it on the primary CTA fill alone, with #E6F3FE as a desaturated echo for the secondary action, over threading brand color through headings and iconography
taste.reason: Color as decoration teaches the reader that color means nothing; color spent only on the next action means a first-time visitor never has to ask what to click
evidence: #0075DE covers 0.2% of surface across exactly 3 elements
body text rgba(0,0,0,0.898), muted #615D59, no chromatic text anywhere

taste.name: Warm Paper, Cool Action
taste.trigger: When choosing the neutral ramp for backgrounds, secondary surfaces, and muted text
taste.decision: Chose warm-tinted neutrals under a cool accent over a hue-neutral gray scale
taste.reason: Warm neutrals read as paper stock rather than unlit screen, which is the right feeling for a product people write documents in, and the warm/cool split makes a 0.2%-coverage blue punch harder than its area should permit because it is the only cool thing on the page
evidence: #615D59 is R97 G93 B89, an 8-point warm spread
shadows stay pure rgba(0,0,0,x) with no hue tint

taste.name: Optical Spacing Beats Grid Purity
taste.trigger: When setting padding inside buttons, chips, and nav items where a strict 8px grid prescribes 8px or 16px
taste.decision: Chose 3px, 5px, 6px, and 10px inside components tuned to the wrapped text, while keeping macro layout strictly 8-based, over one grid governing every value
taste.reason: An 8px grid applied to a 14px button label produces padding that measures correct and looks loose; the reader never sees the grid, only whether the label sits centered in its container
evidence: 6px appears 54x and 3px 46x, statistically tied with 8px at 55x
section values stay pure: 24px x29, 96px x4, 64px x3, footer 80px 0 24px
